newsitem.title: USA: Hilton may drop ITT bid if core hotels are sold.
newsitem.headline: Hilton may drop ITT bid if core hotels are sold.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp. Chief Financial Officer Matthew Hart Wednesday said Hilton may walk away from its $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid for ITT Corp. if ITT sells its core hotels and gaming properties.

"In our view this is an asset play, and if the company sells all the assets, obviously there is nothing for us to buy," Hart said. "To the extent they continue to burn the house down, we might not pursue it at all."
Hilton launched its bid in late January. ITT quickly rejected the offer and began selling non-core assets in an effort to raise cash and focus its business on its Sheraton hotels and Caesars casinos.

Recently, however, ITT has started to consider selling some of its premier hotel properties under an innovative management structure that could prevent Hilton from owning or managing them even if Hilton were to acquire ITT.

Hart, speaking at the Oppenheimer Gaming and Lodging conference here, said Hilton probably would not make a decision on ending its offer until after ITT schedules its annual meeting, which Hilton expects will occur sometime in October.

If ITT holds the meeting in October, it would have to schedule it 30 days in advance, or at some point in September. At that time, Hilton will evaluate what ITT owns and does not own and adjust its $55-a-share bid or perhaps even walk away from the deal altogether, Hart said.
He said in all likelihood Hilton will make a bid for ITT's remaining assets because he doesn't think ITT has enough time to sell all its assets before it calls a meeting.

ITT has about 425 hotels. It owns 72 and franchises or manages the rest. According to people familar with ITT, the company recently received some inquiries about possibly selling some of its premier hotels under a deal that would allow ITT to retain a management contract with the new owners.

The deals, which involve such full-service hotels like the St. Regis in New York and the Phoenician in Arizona, could raise as much as $1.5 billion in cash for ITT, giving the company a total of nearly $5 billion from asset sales.
Analysts said the cash could be used to buy back stock or finance a special dividend to shareholders.
Earlier, ITT sold its stake in French Telecommunications company Alcatel Alsthom for $830 million and announced the sale of its share of Madison Square Garden Inc. for $650 million.

Hart said Hilton probably would have made similar moves if ITT had agreed to negotiate a merger with Hilton. But ITT's recent announcement of a $200 million sale of five hotels to Felcor Suites Hotels Inc. has Hilton concerned because it suggest ITT is willing to sell core hotel assets, too.

By selling hotels, especially the full-service hotels, ITT would be unloading exactly the assets Hilton wants to buy. Moreover, it would seemingly contradict ITT's stated goal to increase its returns to shareholderes by focusing on hotel properties.
ITT declined to comment on whether it will sell the premier hotels.
